newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai baht weaker after bank sets reference rate.
newsitem.headline: Thai baht weaker after bank sets reference rate.

text.p: The Thai baht weakened on Thursday morning from earlier levels after the central bank's announcement of the baht/dollar reference rate at 27.383.
The baht moved out to 29.20/29.90 per dollar offshore from 29.00/29.20 when the rate was set. Onshore the baht was quoted at 27.50/28.50 per dollar against 27.00/27.00 when the rate was set.
The Thai government on Wednesday allowed the baht to float after 13 years of baht fixing against a basket of currencies donominated by the dollar.
Trade was thin and lacked direction onshore as domestic traders digested the reference rate.

"We are working it all out now but I think trade still lacks direction. It is very quiet and I think is maybe quiet onshore for the rest of the day as people are waiting to see what will happen," said a senior dealer at a major commercial bank.
The offshore baht was steady earlier in the day before the reference rate was announced. At 0030 GMT the offshore market quotes from Australia had the currency at 29.00/30.00.
